title: Why Did Australia Fight a War Against Emus?
hook: Australia declared war on emus and lost?
script: Did you know in 1932, the Australian military actually declared war on emus and lost? After World War I, soldiers settled in Western Australia, but a massive drought brought 20,000 emus to their farms, destroying crops. Farmers, many ex-servicemen, asked for military help. So, Major G.P.W. Meredith and his team, armed with machine guns, were sent to cull the birds. What followed was an absolute disaster. The emus, surprisingly agile and organized, used guerrilla tactics, scattering at the first sign of danger. They were incredibly resilient, often shrugging off multiple bullet hits. Soldiers struggled with jammed guns and the sheer speed of the birds. Despite firing thousands of rounds, the official count of emus killed was a mere few hundred. The operation was quickly deemed a failure by the media and public. The military ultimately retreated, admitting defeat to the flightless birds. This incredible true story shows how the Australian military actually declared war on emus and lost.
